LESSON: KENYAN FOLK SONGS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Performing
Topic 2.1: Kenyan Folk Songs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenyan Folk Songs, part of Performing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How does exposure to various performances influence an individual’s response to folksongs? 2. Why are Kenyan folk songs important in society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. in pairs or purposive groups, listen to or watch performances of Kenyan folk songs, discuss/mime the characteristics. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication,

2. source from virtual or physical spaces to select Kenyan folk songs with 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. in pairs or purposive groups, listen to or watch performances of Kenyan folk songs, discuss/mime the characteristics. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication,
2. source from virtual or physical spaces to select Kenyan folk songs with 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenyan Folk Songs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner listens critically to Kenyan folksongs and identifies their

characteristics.

• Citizenship: The learner appreciates listening to and performing folksongs from different social cultural groups in

Kenya.

• Digital Literacy: The learner uses digital devices to record own performances to share with others.

Values:
• Patriotism: The learner appreciates performing folksongs from different Kenyan communities.

• Unity: The learner collaborates with peers to perform Kenyan folksongs.

• Responsibility: The learner makes appropriate use of digital devices when recording and uploading music

performances.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Safety and security: The learner takes precaution while interacting with digital devices as they record and share the

performances with peers for feedback.

38

• Self-esteem: The learner gains confidence as they perform Kenyan folksongs before an audience.

Suggested Learning Resources

Traditional instruments, Portfolios, Anecdotal records, Song book, ICT devices, Internet connectivity, Props and costumes,

Resource persons, Audio/visual recordings of Kenyan folk songs and Text books
